answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the beacon of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. The design leans on time-locked work history, capped per identity per epoch, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. Each submission hangs on the oasis of a task receipt, and the vine is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter.
